 Sanders Named General Manager for Wolfpack Football
 11/16/2026 8:36:00 AM | Football
 Share: McMurray Family Director of Athletics Boo Corrigan and head coach Philip Rivers have announced that Jatavis Sanders has accepted the role of General Manager for the NC State Football program. Sanders brings a wealth of recruiting expertise to his new position, most recently serving as Director of Recruiting at Alabama.
"I'm excited that Jatavis is going to be our general manager," said Rivers. "He's gained great experience and knowledge throughout his career and knows how to navigate what college football is today. I'm excited for us to work together every day and be united in our vision to pursue victory one day at a time." 
Sanders joined the Crimson Tide staff in 2024, where he served as the primary liaison between the program and high school football coaches, working to build and manage relationships with players, parents and other recruiting contacts across the country. He assisted in the organization and maintenance of the Crimson Tide's recruiting board. He played a key role in bringing the nation's third-ranked signing class in 2025 according to 247's composite rankings, while the 2026 class was ranked second nationally.
"This is such an amazing opportunity and blessing for me and my family to return to NC State," said Sanders. "I will work hard to make an impact on the guys in the building and help build a championship-caliber team and culture alongside my former teammate, Philip Rivers, who has a clear vision for this program. I'm grateful to Boo Corrigan for having the trust and confidence in me for this role and I'm excited to get to work."
Sanders, who played at NC State from 1999-2000 and was in the same quarterback room with the Pack's new head coach during his freshman campaign, served as the Director of Recruiting for the Wolfpack in 2023, leading the Wolfpack's recruiting operations. In 2022, he served as the program's director of scouting.
Under his guidance, NC State brought in the nation's 28th-ranked recruiting class in the 2024 cycle, the program's highest-rated recruiting class in 12 years. As Director of Scouting, he evaluated talent and supported the development of recruiting strategies across key regions.
From 2018-22, the Stone Mountain, Ga., native was the Director of Recruiting for the WIllie Anderson Lineman Academy, an Atlanta-based training program. In that role, he consulted with clients and evaluated game film to provide insight into the college football recruiting process.
Sanders gained coaching experience as the co-offensive coordinator and running backs coach at Norcross (Ga.) High School from 2017-22. From 2013-17, he was the offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach at Arabia Mountain High School.
After two years at NC State, Sanders transferred to East Tennessee State, where he earned his bachelor's degree in 2003. He completed his master's in business administration in 2009 and obtained his teaching certificate from the University of Georgia in 2012.
Sanders and his wife, Danyel, have three children: Elijah (23), Arianna (17) and Josiah (9).
